failure_summary.description: Follow-up constraints triggered fresh or broad searches instead of using compatible cached results, or caused unaffected domains to be searched again.
Results were not assigned and saved correctly, including inline calls, missing cache writes, undefined variables, or saving a tool function instead of its result.
Agents inferred unspecified party sizes or mapped criteria to the wrong field, such as treating a state abbreviation as a city.
A round-trip return was encoded as an outbound arrival date instead of a separate reverse-direction flight search.
Agents added searches or nearest-result calls for domains not changed or requested by the latest turn.

patch.reasoning: Most observed errors already violate explicit cache, argument-mapping, flight-leg, and save-the-result instructions, so repeating those rules would not patch a skill gap. The proximity guidance does not clarify how to handle a newly named anchor when the cache contains only broad category results; the added rule makes that scope distinction explicit while preserving valid cached results from other domains.

edits.target: - When the user requests proximity, use the relevant hotel and attraction or restaurant results with `search_nearest`. Set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants prioritized.
edits.content: - If the user names a specific attraction, restaurant, or hotel as the proximity target, make sure the results passed to `search_nearest` are scoped to that named entity. Reuse cached results only when their query scope or summary establishes that they include the target; a general city- or category-level result is not sufficient evidence. Otherwise, run a focused search using the exact name in the appropriate name field, assign and cache its result, and reuse any already-compatible results from the other domain.
